title: Securing Your Cloud: Azure Security Configurations Every Business Should Know
excerpt: Secure your cloud with proven Azure security configurations like identity management, MFA, RBAC, network security, and data protection best practices.

toc.text: Secure Sensitive Data with Microsoft Purview Information Protection

html:
Microsoft offers a range of cloud services and AI solutions to businesses in the form of Azure, and as per the report, 38% organizations around the world access this platform to take their business from local to global. Moreover, as per the recent report of the collaboration between OpenAI and Microsoft Azure, it signifies that businesses can get a range of Azure security features embedded with AI to automate their operations and give the utmost experience to customers.

Undoubtedly, Microsoft Azure offers a safe and secure cloud platform where you can keep your assets, but accessing and utilizing the security components will help you add a layer of security to your credentials. In this article, you will get to know about the Azure security configuration that you can implement to secure your assets.

Azure Identity Access Management

Azure cloud security offers an identity access management feature that comes with Azure hosting. This feature ensures that the authentic person is accessing your resources. With this feature, you can set permission for users to access a set of resources. Now, let’s see the key components available in Microsoft Azure security and an efficient way to configure them to enhance your assets’ security .

Multi-factor Authentication

Multi-factor authentication is a key security component that you can utilize to prevent unauthorized access by users. To get the most from this Azure cloud security, you need to create a conditional access policy in Microsoft Entra ID and thereafter configure the same.

Create Conditional Access Policy

  • First and foremost, you need to sign in to Microsoft Azure using your credentials.
  • Move to Conditional Access, followed by the Security section, and then reach the Overview section. Here at the top of the page, you will find Create a new policy section, click on it.
  • Now, enter the name of the policy and then select the number of users or workload identity in the Assignments section.
  • Scroll down the page to reach the section indicating ‘what does this policy apply to’ and here you need to choose ‘Users and Groups’.
  • Now choose the newly created policy from the ‘Select’ section and start configuring it.

Configure Apps For MFA

After creating a conditional access policy, you need to configure which apps you would like to secure via multi-factor authentication, and for the same, follow the steps listed below.

  • In your conditional access policy page, you will find the Cloud apps or action section, move to the section featuring ‘Select what this policy applies to’ and select the cloud apps.
  • Thereafter, move to the Include section and click on select apps.
  • In the Select section, you will find a range of cloud apps; select Microsoft Azure Management and then click on the Select button.

Give Access To Users

To give access control to users, you need to configure MFA, and the detailed steps are listed below.

  • In your new conditional access policy page, you will find the Access Control section, and here, Grant will be featured, just click on it and select the value.
  • Thereafter, move to the Grant section, select Grant access, and ensure to click on the checkbox stating, ‘Require multifactor authentication’.
  • Now, you need to activate the policy, and for that, move to the Enable policy section.
  • Here you will find three options, i.e., Request-only, On, and Off. You need to click on the On button and further click on the Create button.

Azure RBAC

Azure Role-based Access Control comes under the Azure security best practices that you should follow. It is a security feature that gives you the flexibility to control your resources, such as who will access your resources and what kind of resources will be accessed, like SQL database, virtual machine, subnets, and more. To give users access to your resources, you need to set up the roles, and for that, follow the steps listed below.

Find Resources

  • First and foremost, you need to sign in to the Azure portal with your credentials.
  • At the top of the dashboard, you will find a search bar, and using this, you need to find the Resources by searching for the Scope in the search bar.

Assign Role

  • After selecting the resources, click on the Access Control icon located at the left end of the page.
  • In this page, you will find several tabs located at the top of the page; click on Role assignments and further click on the ‘add role assignment’ button.
  • Thereafter, you will find the search bar featured in the role tab, showing the role names, like Reader, Access Review Operator Service Role, Acr Delete, Acr Push, and more. So, choose the one as per your need and then click on the next button.

Add members

  • To give access to specific users, click on the members tab, located at the top of the page and next to the role tab.
  • In this page, you will find the ‘ Assign access to’ section with two options: click on ‘User, group, or service principal’.
  • Thereafter, you will have to add members, and for that, click on the ‘Select members’ button located parallel to the Members section.
  • After selecting the members, click on the Save button.

Data Protection

Data at rest or transit is secured in the Azure environment, but you will have to configure the key utilities to get the most from Microsoft Azure cloud security. If your data is at rest, then you need to apply the Encryption-at-host feature to enhance your assets’ security. However, if the data is in transit, then you can apply a site-to-site VPN or point-to-point VPN based on the data transit source, i.e., multiple workstations or individual workstations.

Secure Sensitive Data with Microsoft Purview Information Protection

Securing credentials is very important in businesses, and Azure security services feature Purview Information Protection to secure your sensitive information and also prevent your data loss. The detailed steps to configure Purview Information in Azure are provided below.

Sign in to the Azure portal using your credentials and then move to the Search tab to locate Microsoft Purview.

  • After landing on the purview page, click on the Create button, and then fill in the required details featured on the page under the Basics tab.
  • After filling in the details and selecting your current location, click on the Networking tab located beside the Basics tab.
  • Now connect all networks or private endpoints based on your requirements.
  • Thereafter, you will have to configure Event Hubs’ namespaces through Kafka, and you can do the task by entering the Configuration page.
  • Thereafter, move to the Tags section, and in the fields of Name and value, you will have to enter Purview Environment and Production, respectively.
  • Now, click on the Review + Create button and further click on the Create button to create your Purview account.

Network Security

Connect your virtual machines to Azure virtual networks to smooth the communication between the connected devices. In addition, you can control the traffic to your virtual machines by enabling port access features in Azure Network Security. Now, let’s see the different segments of network security that you can configure to enhance your asset security.

Azure WAF

You can protect your web applications from SQL injections and other attacks using Azure cloud security. In addition, you can customize the exclusions and manage the ruleset to enhance your app’s security. So, to create and configure a web application firewall, the steps mentioned below will be helpful for you.

  • Sign in to the Azure portal and then navigate to the top of the portal to find the ‘Create a resource’ tab; click on it and then find WAF and further click on the Create button.
  • After landing on the WAF policy page, you will have to fill in some details in the respective column, like Resource name, Policy name, and Subscription.
  • Thereafter, move to the Association tab, click on the Add association button, and enter the values for Application Gateway, HTTP Listener, and Route Path.
  • Now move to the ‘Review+Create’ section and then click on the Create button.

2. Which industries can benefit from Azure security services?

Azure security services are designed to cover all industries, from Healthcare to Banking, Manufacturing, Logistics, E-Commerce, IT, and more.
